content:
Plan for Phase 71 (cockpit Rules tab) at docs/phases/cockpit-rules-tab.md, on branch phase-71-cockpit-rules-tab.

Decisions to review:
1. SPLIT. 71 is the Rules tab (read everything) plus editing standing orders. Editing tagteam.yaml (targeted line edits, a dry-run diff, a safe key set) becomes a new roadmap entry, 71b, because it is a new engine write path with its own risks. In 71 the tagteam.yaml rows are read-only and name the key to change. Say if you want both halves in one phase.
2. GET /api/rules comes from one server-side payload (cockpit_api.rules_payload). It is file-only, never opens the DB, creates nothing, and is allowed under read-only. Enforced rows: the stop order plus gate / panel / briefer / re-send / auto-escalation, each with a plain-language effect and its source. Advisory: effective().advisory with scope. Presets are defined server-side. The gate's test command is never shown (doctor's rule). An invalid config or orders file becomes a warning, with the values the engine actually uses.
3. POST /api/orders goes through the existing action pattern (_plan / run_action / cli_preview, dry_run shows the exact CLI line) onto `tagteam orders …`, with --by set to the web user. orders_command gains out= so its output can be captured.
4. The tab keeps two visually distinct groups (not by colour alone). Stop is a radio from presets, with the recommended one marked. Advisory has preset chips plus one free-text box. A Project / This run scope toggle. Every write confirms with its CLI line, then reloads.
5. Verification: Python tests for the payload and action, node tests for the JS slice, one real-Chromium check, and a hand look in a real page with screenshots (including the CLI agreeing with the page after writes). Anything only table-tested will be listed.

The 71 / 71b split is reasonable: approve the scope choice of reading engine configuration and editing standing orders now, with safe YAML editing tracked as its own dependent roadmap phase. The existing cockpit action wrapper, explicit enforced/advisory separation, and real-browser verification are appropriate. Two plan details need correction before implementation.

1. Derive engine rows from the runtime resolution rules, not raw get_*_spec helpers (docs/phases/cockpit-rules-tab.md:50-86). Those getters explicitly require validation and do not necessarily describe what runs. A read-only check confirmed gatekeeper enabled=true with scope='invalid' gives get_gatekeeper_spec.enabled=True but resolve_gatekeeper.enabled=False. Likewise watcher resend_minutes=3 with an unknown key gives get_watcher_spec=3, whereas _watch_locked rejects the block and uses 15. Panel/briefer resolution also checks more than the basic getters (for example missing lens briefs/provider availability). Specify shared runtime resolvers, or shared file-only resolution factored from those paths, and test the rows against actual runtime outcomes for invalid blocks. Preserve valid independent blocks when another block is invalid. Include applicable cycle types/phase restrictions and configured checks in the prose: the current example 'Gate before every review' / 'Tests, scope and plan-doc checks' is false for this project's impl-only gate and for scope-disabled or tests-unconfigured gates. The page must distinguish configured policy from a running watcher's previously loaded settings if it does not observe that runtime snapshot.

2. Separate the effective stop policy from the value being edited at each scope (lines 70 and 110-113). The payload supplies only effective stop and run_override, but no saved project stop; the two-option editor also has no specified project-unset control despite success criterion 3. With project stop=phase and run stop=roadmap (or a full-roadmap run-mode), effective stop remains roadmap after a project edit. Binding both scope selections to effective.value would show the wrong saved setting or make a successful change appear to revert. Expose the saved project and run stop values, including unset/inherit, alongside the effective value/source. Define how scope switching, unsetting just a stop order, and clearing all run overrides differ; a stop-only unset must keep that run's advisory notes. Show when a higher-precedence run choice overrides a project edit. Add browser/API criteria for project phase + run roadmap, run-mode roadmap without an explicit stop override, and stop-unset with advisory notes present.

No tests run for this plan review; inspected the existing config resolvers, watcher setup, orders API and cockpit action path. No advisory standing orders or interjections applied.

Both r1 findings are addressed in docs/phases/cockpit-rules-tab.md (last commit on the branch).

1. Engine rows come from the runtime resolvers, not the getters. gate = gatekeeper.resolve_gatekeeper; panel = panel.resolve_panel (validation plus lens-brief and provider resolution); briefer = briefer.resolve_briefer (plus provider resolution); re-send = a new config.resolve_watcher(), factored out of watcher._watch_locked so the watcher and the page share one resolution, with an invalid block giving the default 15 exactly as today; auto-escalation = cycle.STALE_ROUND_LIMIT. Each row has its own resolver, so an invalid block never hides a valid one. Resolver problems become row warnings that say the feature is OFF. The prose follows the resolved spec: which cycle types (for example "implementation reviews only"), when the gate runs (at submission versus in the watcher), which checks are active (tests configured or not, scope on or off, plan-doc), the panel's phases restriction, and never the test command. Configured versus running: each row carries `applies` (each submission / each approval / when the watcher starts). When the heartbeat shows a running watcher that started before tagteam.yaml's mtime, the payload flags watcher_stale_config and the page says the running watcher uses its earlier settings. It does not claim to know them. New criteria 8 (runtime-outcome tests, including your two concrete cases plus panel, briefer, the independent-block case and the check prose) and 10 (a stale-config heartbeat fixture).

2. Saved versus effective stop. The payload now has stop.{effective, source, project, run, run_mode_roadmap, project_shadowed_by}. The scope toggle picks which SAVED value the radio shows (project or run), never the effective one. There are three options: phase, roadmap, and Not set — inherit. The effective line sits above the editor. When a project edit is shadowed by a run choice or by run mode, the editor says the project setting applies from the next run, so an edit never looks like it reverted. "Not set" on This run = `orders stop --unset --run`, which keeps that run's notes. "Clear this run's overrides" = `orders clear --run`, a separate action whose confirmation says it removes the stop and the notes. New criterion 9 (a)–(d) covers, through the API and in the real page: project phase + run roadmap; a full-roadmap run without a stop override; a stop unset with run notes present; clear-run.

The split to 71/71b is kept, as you agreed.

Approved docs/phases/cockpit-rules-tab.md at a7ee220. Both r1 findings are resolved: engine rows use shared runtime resolution and describe applicability/checks, while the stop editor exposes saved project/run values separately from effective policy and distinguishes stop-unset from clearing all run overrides. Criteria 8-10 cover invalid independent config blocks, scope precedence, preservation of run notes, and the configured-versus-running distinction. The 71/71b split remains appropriate.

Implementation note for criterion 10: beat_view currently returns classification/ages, not started_at; that timestamp is in read_beat's record. Use the guarded heartbeat reader (or expose the timestamp through the shared view) while keeping liveness classification in beat_view; do not assume started_at is already a returned field.

Reviewed the revision against runtime resolvers and heartbeat APIs. No tests run for this plan review. No advisory standing orders or interjections applied. No remaining blocking findings.
